title: Oxidation and reduction

concepts.label: spectator ion
concepts.definition: An ion that is present in the solution but comes out of the reaction unchanged, such as sulfate when zinc reacts with copper sulfate.

concepts.label: net ionic equation
concepts.definition: The equation with the spectator ions left out, showing only what changes: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.

concepts.label: redox reaction (electron transfer)
concepts.definition: A reaction in which electrons pass from one particle to another; equivalently (step 8), one in which oxidation numbers change.

concepts.label: oxidation = losing electrons
concepts.definition: Loss of electrons by a particle; its charge (or oxidation number) goes up.

concepts.label: reduction = gaining electrons
concepts.definition: Gain of electrons by a particle; its charge (or oxidation number) goes down. Always paired with an oxidation.

concepts.label: half-reaction
concepts.definition: One side of a redox reaction written alone with its electrons shown, e.g. Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ (oxidation) or Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu (reduction); electrons released must equal electrons taken.

concepts.label: oxidising agent
concepts.definition: The reactant that takes electrons from another, thereby oxidising it, and is itself reduced (Cu²⁺, Cl₂, O₂).

concepts.label: reducing agent
concepts.definition: The reactant that gives electrons to another, thereby reducing it, and is itself oxidised (Zn, Na, Al).

concepts.label: oxidation number
concepts.definition: The charge an atom would have if every shared electron were assigned to the more electronegative atom; a bookkeeping label written sign first (+2, −2), not a real charge.

concepts.label: oxidation-number rules
concepts.definition: Shortcuts: pure element 0; single-atom ion = its charge; group 1 +1, group 2 +2, F −1; H +1 and O −2 in almost all compounds; all numbers sum to the total charge.

concepts.label: redox = oxidation numbers change
concepts.definition: Oxidation is a rise in oxidation number, reduction a fall; electrons moved = change in number × atoms that changed; no change anywhere means not redox.

namedOnly: shared electron pair / covalent bond (described as 'sharing', taught in Silicon and light)
peroxide (O at −1) and metal hydride (H at −1) as named exceptions
permanganate, dichromate, lead dioxide (only as oxidation-number exercises)
acid (zinc in HCl appears in the capstone; taught in The activity series)
precipitation (AgCl 'white solid forms', as the non-redox contrast)
galvanic cell, alkaline cell, fuel cell (pointers only)
summary: Running example: a zinc strip in copper sulfate solution, Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, seen first in a beaker (sulfate as spectator), then as two electrons hopping in one collision, then split into half-reactions and roles (Zn = reducing agent, Cu²⁺ = oxidising agent). Oxidation numbers are introduced through water (shared electrons handed to the more electronegative atom), then five rules and 'number up = oxidised'. Capstone: an oxidation-number sandbox with 7 reactions (Zn/CuSO₄, Na/Cl₂, Zn/HCl, H₂/O₂, thermite, the alkaline-cell reaction Zn + 2MnO₂ → ZnO + Mn₂O₃, and a non-redox AgNO₃ + NaCl trap). Hooks for later lessons: the two half-reactions of Zn/Cu²⁺ (galvanic cell), electrons-lost = electrons-gained (balancing), Cu + 2Ag⁺ and Fe + Cu²⁺ (activity series), Mn +4 → +3 and Pb +4 (batteries).

sources.title: OpenStax, Chemistry 2e, §17.1 Review of Redox Chemistry
Karen, McArdle, Takats (2016), Comprehensive definition of oxidation state (IUPAC Recommendations 2016)
